questions.question: The physiological state which decreases appetite and indicates the feeling of fullness is known as _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**satiety**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Satiety** is the physiological state of feeling full or satisfied, leading to a decreased desire to eat.
 
• It is regulated by complex interactions between the gastrointestinal tract, the brain, and hormones such as **leptin** and **ghrelin**.
 
• Satiety is critical for maintaining energy balance and preventing overeating, contributing to healthy body weight.
 
• Foods rich in fiber, protein, and healthy fats are known to enhance satiety by slowing digestion and promoting prolonged feelings of fullness.
 
• The hypothalamus, a part of the brain, plays a central role in integrating signals related to hunger and satiety.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Leptin**

 
 
• A hormone produced by fat cells (adipocytes) that signals the brain to reduce appetite and increase energy expenditure.
 
• Leptin resistance, often seen in obesity, can impair satiety signals and lead to overeating.
 
 
 
• **Ghrelin**
 
 
• Known as the "hunger hormone," ghrelin is secreted by the stomach when it is empty to stimulate appetite.
 
• Levels of ghrelin decrease after eating, contributing to feelings of satiety.
 
 
 
• **Hypothalamus**
 
 
• A region of the brain responsible for regulating hunger and satiety through neural and hormonal signals.
 
• It integrates information from hormones like leptin, ghrelin, insulin, and peptide YY to maintain energy homeostasis.
 
 
 
• **Role of Fiber in Satiety**
 
 
• Dietary fiber slows gastric emptying, prolonging the digestion process and promoting feelings of fullness.
 
• High-fiber foods like vegetables, fruits, and whole grains are often recommended for weight management.
 
 
 
• **Satiety vs. Hunger**
 
 
• Hunger is the physiological need for food, driven by energy deficits, while satiety is the state of being satisfied after eating.
 
• Both states are essential for energy regulation and are influenced by a variety of internal and external factors.

questions.question: According to Census 2011, what was the percentage of Uttar Pradesh population of the total population of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4 (16.5%)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to Census 2011, the population of Uttar Pradesh constituted **16.5%** of the total population of India.
 
• Uttar Pradesh had the largest population among all Indian states, with a population count of **approximately 199.81 million**.
 
• The total population of India in Census 2011 was recorded as **1.21 billion**.
 
• Uttar Pradesh's demographic dominance significantly impacts national policies and electoral outcomes due to its population size.
 
• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years, and Census 2011 was the 15th National Census exercise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census 2011:**

 
 
• Census 2011 was conducted by the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• This census recorded key demographic data such as population, literacy rate, sex ratio, and urban-rural distribution.
 
• It is considered the most comprehensive data collection exercise in India.
 
• The literacy rate in India as per Census 2011 was 74.04%, and the sex ratio was 943 females per 1000 males.
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh Population Impact:**
 
 
• Uttar Pradesh has 80 Lok Sabha seats, the highest among all states, making it politically significant.
 
• The state's large population places immense pressure on infrastructure, healthcare, and education systems.
 
• It is the most populous state in India, and its population growth has implications for resource allocation and governance.
 
 
 
• **India's Population Distribution:**
 
 
• India's population is unevenly distributed across states, with Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Bihar among the most populous.
 
• Smaller states such as Sikkim and Goa have much lower population counts.
 
• Population density varies widely, with states like Bihar having high density and others like Arunachal Pradesh having low density.
 
 
 
• **Future Census Developments:**
 
 
• The next Census will likely focus on integrating digital data collection methods to improve accuracy.
 
• Population trends observed in the Census help shape long-term national strategies for economic and social development.

questions.question: In geology, Sima (the lower layer of Earth's crust) is made of an assemblage of rocks rich in ________ and magnesium. These two minerals are the most abundance minerals in the oceanic crust.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Silicate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Sima** refers to the lower layer of Earth's crust, which is primarily found beneath the oceanic crust.
 
• It is rich in **silicate** minerals, which are compounds of silicon and oxygen, along with significant amounts of magnesium.
 
• Silicate minerals are the most abundant mineral group in Earth's crust, comprising over 90% of its composition.
 
• Oceanic crust is predominantly made of basalt, which is composed of silicate minerals such as pyroxene and plagioclase feldspar.
 
• The term "Sima" is derived from the first letters of "silica" and "magnesium," indicating its composition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Silicate Minerals**

 
 
• Silicates are categorized into different groups based on their crystal structure, including nesosilicates, inosilicates, phyllosilicates, and tectosilicates.
 
• Examples of silicate minerals include quartz, feldspar, mica, olivine, and pyroxene.
 
• These minerals are essential components of rocks and play a significant role in shaping Earth's geological processes.
 
 
 
• **Oceanic Crust Composition**
 
 
• The oceanic crust is thinner and denser than continental crust, with a thickness of about 5-10 km.
 
• It is mainly composed of basaltic rocks, which are rich in silicate minerals.
 
 
 
• **Basalt**
 
 
• Basalt is a fine-grained igneous rock that forms from the rapid cooling of lava at Earth's surface.
 
• It is rich in iron and magnesium-bearing silicate minerals.
 
 
 
• **Crustal Layers**
 
 
• Earth's crust is divided into two main layers: the upper continental crust (rich in silica and aluminum, termed "Sial") and the lower oceanic crust (rich in silica and magnesium, termed "Sima").
 
• Sima forms the foundation of Earth's ocean basins.

questions.question: Which Act, introduced in 1861, established a legal framework for the governance of British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Councils Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Councils Act of 1861 established a **legal framework** for the governance of British India, allowing Indians to participate in legislation.
 
• It marked a significant step toward **representative governance** by introducing legislative councils in India.
 
• The Act empowered the Governor-General to **create new provinces** and appoint Lieutenant Governors for them.
 
• It restored the legislative power of the provinces, enabling **local self-governance** at provincial levels.
 
• The Act allowed the inclusion of **non-official Indian members** in legislative councils, though their participation was limited.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indian Councils Act 1892**

 
 
• This Act expanded the powers of legislative councils, allowing them to discuss budgets and ask questions.
 
• It increased the representation of Indians in the legislative councils, strengthening their role in governance.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act 1909 (Morley-Minto Reforms)**
 
 
• Introduced separate electorates for Muslims, laying the foundation for communal representation in India.
 
• Increased Indian representation in legislative councils further, including elected members.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms)**
 
 
• Introduced the concept of dyarchy, dividing provincial subjects into reserved and transferred categories.
 
• Marked a major step towards self-governance in India by expanding participation in administration.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1935**
 
 
• Proposed the establishment of an All-India Federation and introduced provincial autonomy.
 
• It was the longest act passed by the British Parliament for India, forming the basis for the Constitution of India.

questions.question: In 1950, besides the chief justice of India, what was the number of other judges in the Supreme Court of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seven**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• At the time of its establishment in 1950, the Supreme Court of India consisted of the **Chief Justice of India** and **seven other judges**, making a total of eight judges.
 
• This composition of the Supreme Court was prescribed under the provisions of the **Constitution of India, Article 124(1)**.
 
• The number of judges in the Supreme Court, including the Chief Justice, has been increased over the years through various amendments due to the increasing workload.
 
• The first Chief Justice of India was **H. J. Kania**, who served from January 26, 1950, to November 6, 1951.
 
• The Supreme Court initially functioned from the Parliament House until it moved to its current building in 1958.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Composition of the Supreme Court:**

 
 
• As per Article 124 of the Constitution, the Supreme Court comprises the Chief Justice of India and other judges as prescribed by Parliament.
 
• Over time, the sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges has been increased to meet the growing demands of judicial work.
 
 
 
• **Amendments to the Number of Judges:**
 
 
• The number of judges was increased to 11 in 1956, 14 in 1960, and further expanded in subsequent decades.
 
• As of 2019, the sanctioned strength of the Supreme Court stands at 34 judges, including the Chief Justice of India.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Supreme Court:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court of India is the **highest judicial authority** and the final court of appeal under the Constitution.
 
• It has the power of judicial review to ensure the constitutionality of laws and executive actions.
 
• It also acts as the guardian of the Constitution and protects fundamental rights of citizens.
 
 
 
• **Important Articles Related to the Supreme Court:**
 
 
• **Article 124:** Establishment and composition of the Supreme Court.
 
• **Article 131:** Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in disputes between the Centre and states or between states.
 
• **Article 136:** Special leave to appeal by the Supreme Court.
 
• **Article 141:** The law declared by the Supreme Court is binding on all courts in India.

questions.question: Bholanath Prasanna was associated with which of the following musical instruments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Flute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Bholanath Prasanna was a renowned flautist known for his mastery in playing the **Flute**, a popular Indian classical musical instrument.
 
• He was associated with Hindustani classical music and significantly contributed to its enrichment through his performances and teachings.
 
• The flute, in Indian classical music, is referred to as the **Bansuri** and is known for its melodious and soulful sound.
 
• Bholanath Prasanna trained several notable students, including the legendary flautist **Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia**, who credits him as his mentor.
 
• His expertise and dedication to the flute have left a lasting legacy in Indian music, inspiring many budding musicians.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Flute (Bansuri) in Indian Classical Music**

 
 
• The flute is a wind instrument made of bamboo and is one of the oldest musical instruments in India.
 
• It has a distinct role in both Hindustani and Carnatic classical music traditions.
 
• The Bansuri is often associated with Lord Krishna in Indian mythology, symbolizing divine love and harmony.
 
• In Hindustani music, the Bansuri is primarily used for ragas and has a rich, emotive tonal quality.
 
 
 
• **Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia**
 
 
• A legendary flautist who popularized the Bansuri in international music circles.
 
• He received training under Bholanath Prasanna and later became one of the most celebrated musicians in the field.
 
• Pt. Hariprasad Chaurasia has been honored with numerous awards, including the Padma Vibhushan.
 
 
 
• **Role of Guru-Shishya Parampara**
 
 
• In Indian classical music, the Guru-Shishya tradition plays a pivotal role in the transmission of knowledge.
 
• Bholanath Prasanna exemplified this tradition by mentoring several students, ensuring the continuity of musical heritage.
 
 
 
• **Flute Construction and Playing Technique**
 
 
• The Bansuri is traditionally made from a single hollow bamboo piece with six to eight finger holes.
 
• It requires precise breath control and finger placement to produce the desired notes and embellishments.

questions.question: Article 49 of the Constitution of India deals with which of the following Directive Principles of State Policy?

options.text: To protect all monuments of historic interest and national importance
To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so
To organise village Panchayats as units of self government
To secure just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To protect all monuments of historic interest and national importance**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 49** of the Indian Constitution falls under the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV).
 
• It directs the state to protect monuments, places, and objects of historic and artistic interest that are of national importance.
 
• The state is responsible for preventing any damage, disfigurement, destruction, or removal of such heritage properties.
 
• This provision reflects India's commitment to preserving its rich cultural and historical heritage.
 
• The protection of these monuments is often carried out in collaboration with institutions like the **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP):**

 
 
• Part IV of the Indian Constitution contains the Directive Principles, which serve as guidelines to the state for governance.
 
• They are non-justiciable in nature, meaning they are not enforceable in a court of law.
 
• However, they aim to create a welfare state and ensure social and economic justice.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Survey of India (ASI):**
 
 
• Established in 1861, the ASI is the premier organization for archaeological research and the preservation of cultural heritage.
 
• It functions under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
 
• ASI is responsible for the maintenance and conservation of monuments and sites of national importance.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India:**
 
 
• India has 40 UNESCO World Heritage Sites as of 2023, including cultural and natural sites.
 
• These sites are of significant importance and are protected under international guidelines as well as national legislation.
 
 
 
• **Monuments of National Importance:**
 
 
• These are monuments declared to be of national importance under the Ancient Monuments and Archaeological Sites and Remains Act, 1958.
 
• There are over 3,600 monuments under the protection of the ASI.

questions.question: Who among the following tendered his resignation as the Chairperson of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in July 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Manoj Soni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Manoj Soni** tendered his resignation as the Chairperson of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) in July 2024.
 
• He was appointed as the **Chairperson of UPSC** on 5 April 2022, succeeding Dr. Pradeep Kumar Joshi.
 
• Manoj Soni has had an illustrious career in academics and administration, previously serving as the Vice-Chancellor of two universities in Gujarat.
 
• As the UPSC Chairperson, he oversaw the conduct of prestigious examinations such as the Civil Services Examination, which is crucial for selecting candidates for elite administrative positions in India.
 
• His tenure focused on enhancing transparency and efficiency in the examination process while ensuring equitable opportunities for candidates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC):**

 
 
• UPSC is India's premier central recruiting agency, responsible for appointments and examinations for All India Services and Group 'A' & 'B' of Central Services.
 
• It was established on **1 October 1926**, and its functions are derived from Article 315 to 323 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The UPSC conducts key exams such as the Civil Services Examination (CSE), Indian Forest Service Examination (IFoS), and Engineering Services Examination (ESE).
 
 
 
• **Role of UPSC Chairperson:**
 
 
• The Chairperson leads the commission in formulating examination policies and ensuring their effective implementation.
 
• They play a key role in maintaining the integrity, fairness, and transparency of the recruitment process.
 
 
 
• **Eligibility for UPSC Exams:**
 
 
• Indian citizens aged between 21 to 32 years (general category) are eligible to appear for the Civil Services Examination.
 
• Relaxations in age and attempts are provided for reserved categories as per government rules.
 
 
 
• **Significance of UPSC:**
 
 
• UPSC ensures a merit-based recruitment process for India's administrative, police, and foreign services.
 
• It plays a crucial role in shaping the leadership and governance framework of the country.

questions.question: Acting as a 'medium of exchange' is an important function of ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**money**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Money** serves as a universally accepted medium of exchange, facilitating transactions for goods and services.
 
• It eliminates the inefficiencies of the barter system, such as the need for a double coincidence of wants.
 
• Money also acts as a unit of account, allowing individuals to measure the value of goods and services in a consistent manner.
 
• It functions as a store of value, enabling individuals to save and transfer purchasing power across time.
 
• Modern forms of money include fiat currency, digital currency, and electronic payment systems, all of which are integral to economic operations globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Barter System:**

 
 
• It is an ancient system where goods and services were exchanged directly without the use of money.
 
• The major drawback was the requirement for a double coincidence of wants, making transactions inefficient.
 
 
 
• **Fiat Money:**
 
 
• Fiat money refers to currency that has no intrinsic value but is established as legal tender by government decree.
 
• Examples include paper currency and coins used globally.
 
 
 
• **Digital Currency:**
 
 
• It includes cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and government-backed digital currencies.
 
• Digital currencies leverage blockchain technology for secure and transparent transactions.
 
 
 
• **Functions of Money:**
 
 
• Medium of exchange: Facilitates buying and selling.
 
• Unit of account: Provides a standard measure for pricing goods and services.
 
• Store of value: Maintains its worth over time, allowing savings.
 
• Standard of deferred payment: Enables credit and future payments.

questions.question: The Sangeet Natak Akademi Award carries a purse money of __________, in addition to a Angavastram and Tamrapatra.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹1,00,000**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** is India's highest recognition given to practicing artists for their outstanding contribution in the fields of music, dance, and drama.
 
• The award includes a **cash prize of ₹1,00,000**, along with an Angavastram (a traditional garment) and a Tamrapatra (a copper plaque).
 
• It was instituted in **1952** by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.
 
• The awards are presented annually by the **President of India** in a ceremony that celebrates the contribution of artists in preserving and promoting India's cultural heritage.
 
• The categories under this award include Hindustani and Carnatic music, classical dance forms, traditional/folk/tribal arts, theatre, and puppetry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi:**

 
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in **1953** as an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
 
• It aims to preserve and promote India's diverse cultural expressions in music, dance, and drama.
 
• The Akademi also supports research, documentation, and training in these art forms.
 
 
 
• **Angavastram:**
 
 
• An Angavastram is a traditional Indian stole or shawl, often made of cotton or silk, symbolizing honor and respect.
 
• It is an important cultural garment offered during ceremonies and awards in India.
 
 
 
• **Tamrapatra:**
 
 
• A Tamrapatra is a copper plate engraved with inscriptions or a citation, symbolizing a formal acknowledgment of achievement.
 
• In the context of awards, it represents the enduring recognition of the recipient's contributions.
 
 
 
• **Other Prestigious Awards in Arts:**
 
 
• **Padma Awards:** Recognize distinguished contributions in various fields, including arts.
 
• **Kalidas Samman:** Honors artists for their exceptional work in performing arts.
 
• **Bharat Ratna:** India's highest civilian award, occasionally given for contributions to arts and culture.

questions.question: In which of the following states is the 'Thaipusam' festival held?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Thaipusam** is a Hindu festival celebrated predominantly in the state of **Tamil Nadu**, India.
 
• It is observed during the Tamil month of **Thai** (January-February) on the day of the full moon.
 
• The festival is dedicated to **Lord Murugan** (also known as Kartikeya), the son of Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati, who is revered as the god of war and victory.
 
• Devotees carry **kavadi** (ornate structures) or perform other penance rituals as acts of devotion during the festival.
 
• Major celebrations of Thaipusam take place at temples such as the **Palani Murugan Temple** in Tamil Nadu and the Batu Caves in Malaysia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Murugan:**

 
 
• He is a prominent deity in Tamil culture, also known as Kartikeya, Subramanya, or Skanda.
 
• Murugan is often depicted with a spear (Vel), representing knowledge and wisdom.
 
 
 
• **Kavadi Attam:**
 
 
• This is a ceremonial sacrifice and offering performed by devotees during Thaipusam.
 
• Devotees carry decorated structures, known as kavadi, as an act of devotion to Lord Murugan.
 
 
 
• **Palani Murugan Temple:**
 
 
• One of the most significant pilgrimage sites for Lord Murugan devotees in Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is located on the Palani Hills and attracts thousands of devotees during Thaipusam.
 
 
 
• **Global Celebrations:**
 
 
• Thaipusam is celebrated not only in Tamil Nadu but also in countries with a significant Tamil diaspora, such as Malaysia, Singapore, and Sri Lanka.
 
• The Batu Caves in Malaysia hosts one of the largest Thaipusam celebrations outside India.

questions.question: Which of the following is Russia's highest civilian honour given to the Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi in July 2024?

options.text: Order of St. Andrew the Apostle

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Order of St. Andrew the Apostle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Order of St. Andrew the Apostle** is the highest civilian honor in Russia, established in 1698 by Tsar Peter the Great.
 
• It is awarded for exceptional services to the state and society in Russia or for strengthening international relations with Russia.
 
• Indian Prime Minister **Narendra Modi** was honored with the award in July 2024 for his contributions to fostering strong ties between India and Russia.
 
• The award is named after **St. Andrew, one of the twelve apostles of Jesus Christ**, and is symbolized by a blue sash and a gold insignia.
 
• The honor highlights the importance of India-Russia strategic partnership in areas such as defense, energy, space, and trade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **History of the Order:**

 
 
• It was the first and highest order of chivalry in Russia, created by Peter the Great in 1698 to honor military and civilian merit.
 
• After the fall of the Russian Empire in 1917, the order was discontinued but reinstated in 1998 by the Russian Federation.
 
 
 
• **St. Andrew the Apostle:**
 
 
• St. Andrew was one of Jesus Christ's apostles and is considered the patron saint of Russia.
 
• The order is named after him as a symbol of courage, devotion, and service.
 
 
 
• **India-Russia Relations:**
 
 
• India and Russia have a strong bilateral relationship, with collaborations in defense, space, energy, and trade.
 
• The two countries have a history of supporting each other on global platforms, including the United Nations.
 
 
 
• **Similar International Honors:**
 
 
• PM Narendra Modi has also received other prestigious international awards, such as the UAE's Order of Zayed and the United Nations' Champions of the Earth Award.
 
• These honors recognize his global leadership and contributions to international cooperation.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Mauryan Empire in 322 BCE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta Maurya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** founded the Mauryan Empire in 322 BCE after overthrowing the Nanda dynasty.
 
• He was guided by his chief advisor, **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, who authored the famous political treatise, *Arthashastra*.
 
• The Mauryan Empire was the first major centralized empire in ancient India, with its capital at **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna).
 
• Chandragupta Maurya expanded his empire by defeating Seleucus I Nicator, a general of Alexander the Great, in 305 BCE, and established a treaty through matrimonial alliances.
 
• He later abdicated the throne and embraced Jainism, spending his final years in Karnataka at **Shravanabelagola**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mauryan Empire:**

 
 
• The Mauryan Empire (322 BCE–185 BCE) is considered one of the largest and most powerful empires in Indian history.
 
• It was known for its efficient administration, military prowess, and trade network.
 
 
 
• **Chanakya (Kautilya):**
 
 
• A key figure in the establishment of the Mauryan Empire, Chanakya was a scholar of economics and political science.
 
• He authored the *Arthashastra*, a comprehensive guide on governance, economics, and military strategy.
 
 
 
• **Seleucus I Nicator:**
 
 
• A successor of Alexander the Great, Seleucus attempted to reclaim territories in India but was defeated by Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• As part of the peace treaty, Chandragupta gifted Seleucus 500 war elephants, which played a significant role in Seleucus’ subsequent campaigns.
 
 
 
• **Shravanabelagola:**
 
 
• A historical Jain pilgrimage site in Karnataka where Chandragupta Maurya is believed to have spent his final years as a Jain ascetic.
 
• The site houses the famous monolithic statue of Lord Bahubali (Gommateshwara).

questions.question: How did the Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961) differ from the First in terms of its approach to industrialisation?

options.text: Prioritised private sector over public sector
Continued the focus solely on agriculture
Emphasised the development of heavy industries
Shifted focus from heavy to light industries

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Emphasised the development of heavy industries**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Second Five Year Plan (1956-1961) marked a **shift in focus to rapid industrialisation**, with particular emphasis on the development of heavy industries such as steel, machinery, and engineering.
 
• It was based on the **Mahalanobis model**, which prioritised capital goods industries to create a strong industrial base for the economy.
 
• This plan sought to reduce dependence on imports by promoting self-reliance in industrial production and emphasising the **public sector** as the primary driver of industrial development.
 
• Unlike the First Five Year Plan, which was primarily focused on **agriculture and rural development**, the Second Plan shifted towards industrial growth to achieve long-term economic stability and employment generation.
 
• Prominent industrial projects during this period included the establishment of major steel plants such as Bhilai, Rourkela, and Durgapur, with assistance from countries like the USSR, Germany, and the UK.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahalanobis Model:**

 
 
• Proposed by Indian statistician P.C. Mahalanobis, this model was adopted to prioritise heavy industries for long-term economic growth.
 
• It emphasised investment in the capital goods sector to build the foundation for industrialisation.
 
• The model assumed that industrial growth would indirectly stimulate agricultural growth and overall development.
 
 
 
• **Public Sector Enterprises:**
 
 
• Under the Second Plan, the government took a leading role in industrialisation by establishing public sector units (PSUs).
 
• These PSUs were seen as tools for economic self-reliance and reducing regional inequalities.
 
 
 
• **Focus of the First Five Year Plan:**
 
 
• The First Five Year Plan (1951-1956) concentrated on **agriculture, irrigation, and land reforms** to address food security and rural development.
 
• It was largely inspired by the Harrod-Domar model, focusing on increasing investment to achieve economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Steel Plants and Collaboration:**
 
 
• Bhilai Steel Plant was established with Soviet assistance, Rourkela with German assistance, and Durgapur with British assistance.
 
• These projects were seen as symbols of India’s industrial progress.
 
 
 
• **Economic Goals of the Second Plan:**
 
 
• Self-reliance in industrial production to reduce imports.
 
• Creation of employment opportunities through industrialisation.
 
• Balanced regional development by setting up industries in underdeveloped areas.

questions.question: The Popir dance is performed by the Galo tribe of which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arunachal Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Popir dance is a traditional folk dance performed by the **Galo tribe**, which is indigenous to Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• This dance is typically performed during **harvest festivals** and other significant cultural events in the state.
 
• The Galo tribe is one of the **major tribes in Arunachal Pradesh**, known for its rich cultural heritage and traditional practices.
 
• Popir dance is characterized by **graceful movements, vibrant costumes, and rhythmic music**, showcasing the tribe's deep connection with nature and their traditions.
 
• Arunachal Pradesh is renowned for its diverse tribal communities, and dances like Popir play a crucial role in preserving and promoting their cultural identity.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Galo Tribe:**

 
 
• The Galo tribe is primarily located in the West Siang and East Siang districts of Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• They speak the **Galo language**, which belongs to the Tibeto-Burman language family.
 
• The tribe is known for its practices of sustainable agriculture and reverence for nature.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Tribal Dances of Arunachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• Besides Popir, other tribal dances include **Wancho Dance, Pasi Kongki, and Buiya Dance**.
 
• These dances are performed during festivals, religious ceremonies, and social gatherings.
 
• They often include storytelling elements and rituals that reflect the tribe's way of life.
 
 
 
• **Harvest Festivals in Arunachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• Major harvest festivals celebrated include **Solung, Mopin, and Nyokum.**
 
• These festivals signify gratitude to nature and ancestral spirits for a bountiful harvest.
 
• Dance and music are integral to these celebrations, fostering community bonding.
 
 
 
• **Arunachal Pradesh:**
 
 
• It is India’s northeastern-most state, often referred to as the **"Land of the Rising Sun."**
 
• The state is home to **26 major tribes and over 100 sub-tribes**, making it culturally diverse.
 
• Arunachal Pradesh is known for its scenic beauty, biodiversity, and unique tribal traditions.

questions.question: When did Hans Christian Oersted discover that the flow of electric current in a wire could deflect a nearby magnetic compass needle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1820**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hans Christian Oersted discovered in **1820** that an electric current flowing through a wire produces a magnetic field capable of deflecting a nearby magnetic compass needle.
 
• This finding marked the beginning of the field of **electromagnetism**, bridging the gap between electricity and magnetism.
 
• Oersted demonstrated this effect during a public lecture, showcasing the interaction between electric currents and magnetic fields.
 
• The experiment showed that the magnetic field produced by the current was circular and centered around the wire.
 
• The discovery laid the foundation for subsequent advancements in electromagnetism, including Faraday’s and Maxwell’s work.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electromagnetism:** A branch of physics dealing with the interaction of electric currents and magnetic fields, forming the basis for technologies like electric motors and generators.
 
• **Magnetic Field:** A region around a magnetic material or current-carrying conductor where magnetic forces can be observed.
 
• **Faraday’s Law:** Later developments by Michael Faraday showed that a changing magnetic field could induce an electric current, leading to the principle of electromagnetic induction.
 
• **Maxwell’s Equations:** James Clerk Maxwell unified the concepts of electricity and magnetism into four mathematical equations, forming the foundation of classical electromagnetism.
 
• **Applications:** The principles of electromagnetism are used in various devices, including compasses, electric motors, generators, transformers, and communication technologies.

questions.question: What was the targeted growth rate of the Eleventh Five-year Plan (2007–2012)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Eleventh Five-Year Plan of India (2007–2012) targeted a **GDP growth rate of 9%**.
 
• It focused on **inclusive growth**, aiming to reduce poverty and ensure that economic benefits reached all sections of society.
 
• The plan emphasized investments in agriculture, education, health, and infrastructure to boost growth and improve quality of life.
 
• Though the target was 9%, the actual growth rate achieved was approximately **7.9%**, falling short due to the global financial crisis of 2008.
 
• It was approved under the leadership of then Prime Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**, with Montek Singh Ahluwalia as the Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Five-Year Plans in India**

 
 
• Five-Year Plans were introduced in India in 1951 based on the Soviet model to promote economic development through centralized planning.
 
• These plans were formulated by the **Planning Commission** (later replaced by NITI Aayog in 2015).
 
• The focus of each plan varied, addressing different sectors such as agriculture, industry, education, and health.
 
 
 
• **Inclusive Growth**
 
 
• Inclusive growth refers to economic growth that is distributed fairly across society and creates opportunities for all, especially the marginalized sections.
 
• The Eleventh Plan aimed to bridge disparities in income, education, gender, and regions.
 
 
 
• **Global Financial Crisis of 2008**
 
 
• The crisis began with the collapse of major financial institutions in the United States, causing a ripple effect worldwide.
 
• India's economy was impacted, leading to slower GDP growth during the later years of the Eleventh Plan.
 
 
 
• **Transition to NITI Aayog**
 
 
• The Planning Commission was replaced by **NITI Aayog** in 2015 to adopt a more decentralized and participatory approach to planning.
 
• NITI Aayog focuses on fostering cooperative federalism and preparing long-term strategies for India’s development.

questions.question: Which edition of Kumar Surendra Singh Memorial Shooting Championship 2023 was organised at Bhopal and Trivandrum?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**21st**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **21st edition** of the Kumar Surendra Singh Memorial Shooting Championship 2023 was organized in **Bhopal** and **Trivandrum**.
 
• This championship is an important event in the Indian **shooting sports calendar**, conducted annually to promote shooting talent.
 
• It is named after **Kumar Surendra Singh**, a former President of the National Rifle Association of India (NRAI), who contributed significantly to the development of shooting sports in the country.
 
• The event includes competitions across various categories such as **rifle, pistol, and shotgun shooting**, attracting top shooters from across the nation.
 
• It serves as a platform for aspiring shooters to showcase their skills and gain recognition at the national level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Rifle Association of India (NRAI):**

 
 
• NRAI is the governing body for shooting sports in India, established in 1951.
 
• It is affiliated with the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) and oversees the development of shooting disciplines in the country.
 
 
 
• **Shooting Sports in India:**
 
 
• Shooting has gained significant popularity in India, especially after performances by Indian shooters in events like the Olympics and ISSF World Cups.
 
• Prominent Indian shooters include **Abhinav Bindra** (India's first individual Olympic gold medalist), **Manu Bhaker**, and **Saurabh Chaudhary**.
 
 
 
• **Types of Shooting Events:**
 
 
• Shooting events are broadly categorized into **rifle, pistol, and shotgun disciplines**.
 
• Each discipline involves different techniques, equipment, and competition formats.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Championships:**
 
 
• National-level championships like the Kumar Surendra Singh Memorial Shooting Championship help in identifying and nurturing talent for international competitions.
 
• They also provide athletes with exposure to competitive environments and help improve their performance under pressure.

questions.question: As per Census 2011, which north-eastern state has the highest literacy rate?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Census 2011, **Mizoram recorded the highest literacy rate among north-eastern states** at 91.33%.
 
• The literacy rate of Mizoram is significantly higher than the **national average of 74.04%** reported in Census 2011.
 
• Among districts, **Serchhip district** of Mizoram had the highest literacy rate in the state, showcasing a strong emphasis on education.
 
• Mizoram's high literacy rate is attributed to its **effective implementation of education policies** and the cultural emphasis on acquiring knowledge.
 
• Other northeastern states like Tripura and Assam also have commendable literacy rates, but Mizoram leads the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Literacy Rate Definition:**

 
 
• Literacy rate refers to the percentage of people aged 7 years and above who can read and write with understanding.
 
• It is a critical indicator of a region's educational attainment and socio-economic development.
 
 
 
• **Census 2011:**
 
 
• Census 2011 is the 15th National Census conducted by the Government of India.
 
• It provided important demographic, social, and economic data, including literacy rates across states and districts.
 
 
 
• **Factors Contributing to High Literacy Rates in Mizoram:**
 
 
• Efficient implementation of educational policies by the state government.
 
• Strong community participation in promoting education.
 
• Availability of educational infrastructure even in remote areas.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other States:**
 
 
• Kerala recorded the highest literacy rate in India at 93.91%, followed closely by Mizoram among northeastern states.
 
• Other northeastern states like Tripura (87.75%) and Assam (72.19%) also showed notable literacy achievements.

questions.question: With which game is the Indian player R Vaishali associated?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chess**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• R Vaishali is an Indian chess player who has earned the titles of **International Master (IM)** and **Woman Grandmaster (WGM)**.
 
• She is the elder sister of Indian chess prodigy **R Praggnanandhaa**.
 
• Vaishali has represented India at numerous **international chess tournaments**, bringing accolades to the nation.
 
• In 2022, she won a bronze medal with the Indian team in the **Chess Olympiad** held in Chennai.
 
• Her achievements include winning the **World Youth Chess Championship** twice (Under-12 and Under-14 categories).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chess Terminologies:**

 
 
• **Grandmaster (GM):** The highest title awarded by FIDE, the international chess federation.
 
• **International Master (IM):** A title awarded to players below the level of Grandmaster but above other FIDE titles.
 
• **Woman Grandmaster (WGM):** The highest title exclusively for female chess players.
 
 
 
• **Chess Olympiad:**
 
 
• A biennial chess tournament where teams from different countries compete.
 
• India has been emerging as a strong contender in recent editions of the Olympiad.
 
 
 
• **Indian Chess Achievements:**
 
 
• India has produced several renowned players like **Viswanathan Anand**, the first Indian to become a Grandmaster.
 
• Indian chess players have consistently performed well at youth championships, Olympiads, and international events.
 
 
 
• **FIDE:**
 
 
• FIDE stands for Fédération Internationale des Échecs or International Chess Federation.
 
• It is the governing body of international chess competitions and awards titles like GM, IM, and WGM.
